record.title: Inventory denial and merchant spam via soft stock-reservation abuse across self-registered customer accounts
record.description: End-to-end source-verified abuse chain: (1) POST /api/customer-auth/register/ is AllowAny self-service registration guarded only by CustomerRegisterThrottle (scope 'register' = 10/hour keyed by client IP when no customer session exists) with NO captcha — CustomerRegisterView.post never calls verify_captcha, and CustomerRegisterSerializer only requires a unique well-formed email plus a Django-policy password. RegisterCustomerQuery creates the Customer with model defaults is_active=True / email_verified=False and _session_response issues a working customer_access JWT immediately; email verification is never required anywhere in the order path (IsCustomer checks only isinstance+is_active; mails.py:269-272 only skips CUSTOMER lifecycle emails for unverified addresses). (2) POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/orders/ requires only IsCustomer and is throttled by OrderCreateThrottle — a ResilientUserRateThrottle (scope 'store_order_create', rate '10/hour') whose DRF UserRateThrottle.get_cache_key keys on request.user.pk = customer.pk, i.e. PER ACCOUNT, not per IP. One IP minting ~10 accounts/hour therefore yields ~100 orders/hour. (3) The order captcha is deterministic arithmetic (add/sub/mul of small ints, single-use nonce, 5 attempts, >=3s min delay) — a scriptable speed bump, not a bot barrier. (4) Each created order claims SOFT STOCK globally: claimed_quantities sums OrderItem.qty over ALL customers' orders with status=PENDING_PAYMENT and expires_at > now (no customer filter), and _resolve_lines rejects any buyer whose qty exceeds product.stock - claimed. Caps are MAX_QTY=100 per product line and MAX_ITEMS=50 lines per order, so a single order can claim up to 100 units of up to 50 SKUs. expires_at = now + payment_deadline_hours (default 48h, owner-configurable 1..720h via StorePaymentConfig serializer); release is TIME-BASED inside the claimed_quantities query (expires_at__gt=now) — it does NOT depend on the expire_orders cron, refuting the hunter's cron blocker. Sustaining the DoS needs only continuous re-ordering at 10/h/account. (5) Every order fires append_event('created') -> dispatch_order_event: 'created' is in OWNER_NOTIFY_KINDS (synchronous in-app Notification to the store owner) and OWNER_EVENT_KINDS (transaction.on_commit -> Celery -> _owner_new_order_mail SMTP). ~100 fake orders/hour/IP = ~100 owner emails+notifications per hour. Impact: a single scripted IP can keep any stock-controlled low-stock SKU permanently 'sold out' to legitimate buyers (qty > available -> ValidationError 'Stock insuficiente') and spam the merchant's inbox/notifications, at zero cost (orders just expire unpaid).
record.root_cause: Stock reservations are claimed per-order GLOBALLY (claimed_quantities counts every customer's PENDING_PAYMENT orders regardless of owner) while order creation is gated only by a per-customer-pk throttle (10/hour), a scriptable arithmetic captcha, and self-service registration that is itself only IP-throttled at 10/hour with no captcha and no email_verified requirement — there is no per-IP order throttle, no per-store pending-reservation cap, and no verified-principal requirement before stock claims materialize.
record.intended_behavior: Stock claims should require a minimally verified principal (e.g., email_verified) and/or orders should be throttled per-IP in addition to per-account, with a cap on simultaneous PENDING_PAYMENT reservations per store/customer, so anonymous-scale account minting cannot monopolize inventory or flood the merchant.

trace.description: POST /api/customer-auth/register/ — AllowAny self-service registration; throttle_classes=[CustomerRegisterThrottle] (line 229) = scope 'register' 10/hour (settings.py:111) keyed by IP via CustomerRateThrottle.get_cache_key fallback to get_ident when request.customer is None (lines 175-178). No captcha anywhere in the view (post at 231-246).

POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/orders/ — permission_classes=[IsCustomer] only; throttle_classes=[OrderCreateThrottle] (line 125) = ResilientUserRateThrottle scope 'store_order_create' rate '10/hour' (lines 63-67) keyed by request.user.pk = customer.pk via DRF UserRateThrottle.get_cache_key (venv rest_framework/throttling.py:193-202) — per ACCOUNT, not per IP. Captcha verified at line 136 (arithmetic, scriptable).
Requires only isinstance(request.customer, Customer) and customer.is_active — no email_verified, no membership, no per-store check anywhere in the order path.

Sums OrderItem.qty over Order.status=PENDING_PAYMENT AND order.expires_at__gt=now for the given product_ids across ALL customers (lines 286-294) — one global reservation pool; expiry is evaluated in the query, so release does not depend on the expire_orders cron.

available = product.stock - claimed.get(pid, 0); qty > available -> ValidationError — attacker's pending orders exhaust stock for every other buyer. Caps MAX_QTY=100/line, MAX_ITEMS=50 lines (lines 88-89); expires_at = now + payment_deadline_hours, default 48h, owner-set 1..720h (line 464).

Every 'created' event: kind in OWNER_NOTIFY_KINDS -> synchronous in-app owner Notification (lines 35-38, 89-92) AND kind in OWNER_EVENT_KINDS -> transaction.on_commit Celery email -> mails.py:46-49,276-283 _owner_new_order_mail — fake orders spam the merchant inbox and panel.

evidence.description: 'register': '10/hour' — the only gate on self-service customer account minting; keyed by IP for anonymous requests.
CustomerRegisterThrottle scope='register'; get_cache_key (175-178) uses customer.pk if present else IP ident — anonymous registration buckets per IP at 10/h.

OrderCreateThrottle: ResilientUserRateThrottle scope='store_order_create' rate='10/hour' — DRF UserRateThrottle keys authenticated requests by request.user.pk = customer.pk (per account, evadable by minting accounts).
is_active default True, email_verified default False (line 62); is_authenticated property returns True (117-119) so the customer JWT always takes the pk-keyed throttle path.

RegisterCustomerQuery creates the Customer with model defaults and only enqueues a verification email post-commit — tokens are issued immediately (auth_views.py:246 _session_response); nothing requires email_verified to order.
_captcha_question generates deterministic arithmetic (add/sub/mul of small integers); verify_captcha (76-121) enforces only signature+TTL 300s+min 3s+5 attempts — trivially scriptable.
claimed_quantities filter: product_id__in + order__status=PENDING_PAYMENT + order__expires_at__gt=now — NO customer/store-claimant partition; global soft reservation.
available = product.stock - claimed; qty > available -> ValidationError 'Stock insuficiente' — cross-customer stock monopolization.
expires_at = now + deadline_hours (default 48h via DEFAULT_DEADLINE_HOURS line 90; owner-configurable 1..720h per storepayments/serializers/serializers.py:80-83).
OWNER_NOTIFY_KINDS and OWNER_EVENT_KINDS both contain 'created' — every fake order creates an in-app owner notification plus a Celery-queued owner email (mails.py:276-283).

conditions.description: Target store is published with orders_enabled and has stock-controlled products (product.stock not null); low stock makes monopolization cheap — one order can claim up to 100 units of each of up to 50 SKUs.

Register throttle is per-IP (10/h) and order throttle per-account (10/h): a single IP yields ~10 accounts/h -> ~100 orders/h; IP rotation scales linearly. _pinned_ident (throttling.py:14-27) pins REMOTE_ADDR into the bucket so XFF spoofing does not reset it.

Throttles fail open on cache loss (deliberate, throttling.py:64-79) — but the configured 10/h rates already permit the abuse, so enforcement status does not gate exploitability; fail-open only increases attacker throughput.
The owner-email sub-impact requires a running Celery worker + reachable SMTP; the inventory-denial impact is synchronous DB state inside create_order and needs neither.

execution.attacker_perspective: Anonymous internet user running a script against a public DAVENT store with ecommerce orders enabled.
payloads: POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/orders/ {"items":[{"product_id":<pid>,"qty":<stock>}],"shipping_method":"pickup","payment_method":"transfer","challenge_id":"<id>","captcha_answer":"<answer>"} -> 201 (repeat <=10/h per account, rotate accounts at 10/h per IP)
instructions: Enumerate stock-controlled products and their stock via the public catalog endpoints.
Register customer accounts at 10/hour per IP (no captcha; unique disposable emails suffice; session tokens issued immediately).
For each account, fetch an order captcha, wait >=3s, solve the arithmetic question, and POST orders claiming qty=stock for target SKUs (up to 50 lines x 100 units per order).

Repeat continuously: claims last until expires_at (48h default, up to 720h owner-set) and auto-release via expires_at__gt=now — sustained ~10 orders/h/account keeps low-stock SKUs 'sold out' indefinitely.
Observe legitimate buyers receiving 'Stock insuficiente' ValidationErrors and the owner receiving an in-app notification + email per fake order.
execution.observed_result: Source-derived (read-only audit, not executed): every link verified line-by-line — uncaptcha'd IP-throttled registration, per-customer.pk 10/h order throttle, global claimed_quantities across all customers' PENDING_PAYMENT orders, expires_at-based release independent of cron, and per-order owner notification+email dispatch.

remediation.strategy: Gate stock-claiming order creation on a verified principal and bound abuse per origin: (a) require customer.email_verified (or an equivalent verified-contact check) in PublicOrderCreateView/create_order before materializing claims; (b) add a per-IP order throttle alongside the per-account one so account minting does not multiply the budget; (c) cap simultaneous PENDING_PAYMENT reservations per store and/or per customer (e.g., reject create_order when the customer already holds >=N pending orders for the store, and/or when store-wide pending claims exceed a fraction of stock); (d) add captcha (or disposable-email checks) to customer registration; (e) optionally digest owner 'created' notifications/emails instead of one per order.

likelihood.reason: Fully scriptable end-to-end from a single IP (~10 accounts/h -> ~100 orders/h; each order claims up to 100 units x 50 SKUs, so even one account can exhaust low-stock SKUs). Requires a target store with stock-controlled products worth attacking and sustained automation, but cost and skill barrier are minimal.

impact.reason: Blocks legitimate purchase of targeted SKUs for the attack duration (claims auto-release at expires_at <=720h, default 48h, but the attacker sustains with continuous orders) and floods the merchant with order notifications/emails (~100/h/IP). Bounded per store, reversible, no confidentiality/integrity breach or payment fraud.

confidence.reason: Every link re-verified line-by-line in current source. The hunter's three blockers dissolve on inspection: stock release is expires_at-based inside the claimed_quantities query (checkout.py:290), not cron-dependent; the captcha is provably deterministic arithmetic (contact.py:49-65); throttle rates and cache keys are source constants, and the deliberate fail-open only increases attacker throughput rather than gating the abuse.

record.title: Store MP webhook and public order-pay inherit the default 'anon' 100/day per-IP throttle — shared Mercado Pago egress IPs may starve legitimate payment notifications
record.description: StoreMpWebhookView (POST /api/webhooks/store-mp/<slug>/) declares permission_classes=[AllowAny] and authentication_classes=[] but NO throttle_classes, so DRF applies DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES = ResilientAnonRateThrottle + ResilientUserRateThrottle. With no authentication, every request.user is anonymous, so only the 'anon' scope applies: rate '100/day' keyed by client IP into the single cache bucket 'throttle_anon_<ident>' — a scope SHARED by every view that relies on default throttles (the bucket has no per-view component). All Mercado Pago webhook deliveries platform-wide arrive from MP's shared egress infrastructure; if a single egress IP (or the small set MP uses) delivers >100 notifications/day aggregate across ALL DAVENT stores, legitimate signed payment notifications start receiving HTTP 429 before any HMAC/dedup/store logic runs, delaying or dropping order-payment confirmations (MP retries failed deliveries, but a sustained over-cap volume outlasts any finite retry horizon). PublicOrderPayView (POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/orders/<token>/pay/) has the identical exposure on the buyer side (AllowAny, authentication_classes=[], no throttle_classes -> same shared 'anon' bucket; less acute since buyer IPs are diverse, but CGNAT/office NAT could concentrate it). Source-visible facts: the missing throttle_classes, the default classes/rates, the shared per-IP bucket semantics, and that the only nginx limit_req in the repo covers /api/token/ exclusively (docker/web/templates/default.conf.template:10,112-115) — no proxy-layer mitigation for /api/webhooks/*. NOT source-visible: MP's actual webhook egress IP count/distribution, aggregate daily notification volume for the platform, and MP's retry-on-429 policy/horizon — all decisive for whether starvation actually occurs.
record.claimed_root_cause: StoreMpWebhookView and PublicOrderPayView omit throttle_classes, so they inherit DRF's DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES; the anonymous 'anon' scope (100/day) is a single per-IP bucket shared across all default-throttled endpoints platform-wide, and MP webhook egress IPs are shared infrastructure — aggregate webhook volume from one IP can exceed 100/day and 429 legitimate payment notifications.

trace.description: POST /api/webhooks/store-mp/<slug>/ — permission_classes=[AllowAny] (line 110), authentication_classes=[] (line 113), and no throttle_classes attribute on the class -> DRF falls back to api_settings.DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES.

Returns None for authenticated users; for anonymous requests the cache key is 'throttle_anon_<ident>' — one shared bucket per IP across EVERY view using the default anon scope (no per-view component). UserRateThrottle similarly keys 'throttle_user_<pk>'/'throttle_user_<ip>' (lines 193-202).

The 100/day per-IP cap is enforced in APIView.initial -> check_throttles BEFORE StoreMpWebhookView.post runs — a throttled legitimate MP notification gets HTTP 429 and never reaches HMAC verification, dedup, or StoreMpWebhookQuery.

evidence.description: class StoreMpWebhookView(APIView): permission_classes=[AllowAny], authentication_classes=[] — no throttle_classes declared anywhere in the 184-line file.
class PublicOrderPayView(APIView): same pattern — AllowAny, authentication_classes=[], no throttle_classes -> same shared 'anon' bucket for buyer-initiated MP checkout.
DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES applies ResilientAnonRateThrottle + ResilientUserRateThrottle to every view without explicit throttle_classes.

ResilientAnonRateThrottle/ResilientUserRateThrottle are thin _ResilientThrottleMixin wrappers (fail-open on cache loss, lines 64-85) — they inherit DRF's get_cache_key unchanged, so the 'anon' bucket stays IP-keyed and scope-shared.
AnonRateThrottle cache_format % {'scope':'anon','ident':<ip>} — identical key for all default-throttled views; authenticated requests return None (line 175).
Only limit_req_zone exists for zone=api_token applied solely to location = /api/token/ (lines 112-115); /api/ and /api/webhooks/* have no proxy-layer rate limit in the docker deploy.
WEBHOOK_DEDUP_SECONDS=600 and cache.add dedup (lines 165-173) only run AFTER the throttle check — a 429'd delivery is never dedup-recorded, so MP retries re-enter the same exhausted bucket.

blockers: MP webhook egress IP count/distribution and aggregate daily notification volume across ALL DAVENT stores are provider facts not in source — starvation requires >100 deliveries/day (or shared 'anon' bucket consumption by other anonymous traffic from the same IPs) within the 100/day window.

MP's retry behavior on HTTP 429 (retry count, backoff schedule, maximum retry age) is provider-side and not documented in the repo — it determines whether throttling merely delays confirmations or permanently drops them after retry exhaustion.

Production topology is decisive and not fully source-visible: the docker/nginx deploy rate-limits only /api/token/, but the Render blueprint path has no nginx layer at all; whether any edge/WAF rate limiting sits in front in the actual deployment cannot be confirmed from source.
Resilient throttles fail open on cache loss — whether the 'anon' bucket is even enforced depends on production cache health (normal state assumed, but a deployment fact).

validation_plan.local: In a test deployment with a working cache, send 101+ POSTs to /api/webhooks/store-mp/<slug>/ from a single IP (any body — the throttle fires before HMAC) and confirm the 101st returns 429; then alternate requests between the webhook and PublicOrderPayView from the same IP to prove they share the single 'throttle_anon_<ip>' bucket. Repeat with cache stopped to confirm fail-open.
validation_plan.deployment: Inspect production access logs / MP developer panel for webhook delivery counts per day and the source IPs MP uses; determine whether any single egress IP exceeds ~100 deliveries/day aggregate; check MP documentation/support for retry-on-429 semantics and horizon. If volume is material, remediation is to give the webhook a dedicated throttle scope (e.g., throttle_classes=[StoreMpWebhookThrottle] with a high rate like '10000/day' keyed by IP, or ScopedRateThrottle per slug) since HMAC signature — not rate — is the real authentication, and optionally add a matching dedicated scope to PublicOrderPayView.
